rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 End Game 4 Special Tile Overview Collect the most coins to win the game. There are 9 characters in the game. There are 72 cards - all double sided and each character appears 16 times Turn Draw a character tile from the bag. You can either keep the side you see, or flip it and have the other side (but no backflips). Place the tile on that side at the lowest point on a column of your choice. Apply the immediate effect (Yellow). If they are on the highest space of their column, also take the column bonus. If you hold the Treasure Map at the end of your turn, take 1 coin. End Game When one player completes 4 columns, finish off the round, then end the game. Apply end game effects of characters (grey). If using board C, there are also end game bonuses on the board. The player with the most coins wins! Remember, 3 Gunner tiles or more at the end automatically loses! If tied, the player who currently holds the treasure map wins! Scoring FAQ: Swabbies score by number of columns they are in. Multiple swabbies in a single column will not increase your score. Special Tile Dolphin (promo) Tile. If played, this tile allows everyone to flip one tile previously played and use the effect.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Begrudgingly simple. I suspect that one can improve their gameplay if they memorize all the tiles in the game and know which ones have been used (and thus which ones will still eventually come out). But [i]that[/i] game is not one that I'm interested in playing.

[Rating: 1/10] The parrot tile is not well balanced, like who ever gets the most parrot tile wins. I played this game on board game arena and who ever gets the most parrots always win.

[Rating: 2/10] One play on BGA, but it just seemed so boring. Sushi Go is more interesting to me, and I don't even really like Sushi Go. Carcassonne is better too. I just don't see the appeal.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA, love the concept and it is a nice addictive tile placement game. Only marred but completely unbalanced tiles that make luck to powerful.

[Rating: 3/10] a very simple kids game where you pull tiles, decide if you flip it and in which column you slot it way too light and flat barely a game quite silly miserable memory aspect that might come up or not very luck-dependent no player interaction  If you really have/want to, then better play it digitally.

[Rating: 3/10] Barely any decisions. 3 because flipping to the gunner and automatically losing is funny as hell.

[Rating: 3/10] BGA. The SdJ has really fallen on hard times since the heady days of Torres, still the greatest SdJ game in history, and Tikal. This should be in the children's game category. No meaningful decisions, extremely random, zero tension and missing the twist that Knizia has in his best light games that make them good. This is a waste of time and cardboard.

[Rating: 3/10] Feels a lot like Challengers from the previous year(ish) where it's clean enough but kind of feels a little too auto-pilot to not just feel like an "activity" to use a dirty comparison. Too disengaged by the lack of adjacency to really invest in the game of it.
